content.definition: Everything bears the relation to itself, like 'is the same age as'.
If x bears it to y, then y bears it to x, like 'is married to'.
If x bears it to y and y to z, then x bears it to z, like 'is taller than'.

content.text: A relation with all three is an **equivalence relation**.

examples.title: Symmetric but not transitive
lines: If A is within a mile of B, then B is within a mile of A.
A can be within a mile of B, and B of C, while A is two miles from C.

examples.title: Transitive but not symmetric
lines: An ancestor of your ancestor is your ancestor.
If A is an ancestor of B, then B is not an ancestor of A.

question.hint: Chain two steps. Does the first link lead straight to the third?
question.explanation: If A is older than B and B is older than C, then A is older than C. Your mother's mother is not your mother.
